sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.used_for: Section 5, Identifying Yourself as an Associate — the required disclosure wording.
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Policies
sources.used_for: The tag requirement for Special Links, and the price and availability rule.
sources.quote: All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. ... you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Policies — price and availability
sources.used_for: Why no price, rating or stock status appears anywhere on this site.
sources.quote: your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking — affiliate marketing
sources.used_for: Disclosure placement and wording, including why a bare label is not enough.
sources.quote: You should disclose your relationship to the retailer clearly and conspicuously on your site ... As for where to place a disclosure, the guiding principle is that it has to be clear and conspicuous. The closer the disclosure is to your recommendation, the better.

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides — is “affiliate link” an adequate disclosure?
sources.used_for: Why the disclosure strip carries a full sentence and a 'Paid links' label rather than a bare tag.
sources.quote: Consumers might not understand that “affiliate link” means that the person placing the link is getting paid for purchases made through the link. Similarly, a “buy now” button would not be adequate. ... “Paid link” right next to an affiliate link should be an adequate disclosure of the nature of the link.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials
sources.used_for: The regulation behind the FTC guidance above. Linked for the reader; no wording is quoted from it here.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.used_for: Why every Amazon product link carries rel="sponsored nofollow noopener".
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

sources.title: Food Thermometers
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.page_date: no review date shown on the page
sources.used_for: What a food thermometer is for, how accurate it is expected to be, and why the manufacturer's instructions decide placement and insertion depth.
sources.quote: Using a food thermometer is the only reliable way to ensure that foods have been cooked to a safe minimum internal temperature to destroy any harmful microorganisms that may be in the food.
